title: Client-side session proxy — handshake & sync sketch
content:
Quick scratchpad for a client-side (user device) session proxy that mediates between local apps and the Redwood edge/runtime. Mostly thinking through handshake, key sync, and KV/prefix cache invariants. Rough, notes-to-self style.

Purpose:
- Reduce cold-roundtrips for on-device flows by establishing a lightweight trusted session with Redwood Edge.
- Allow short-lived local proxies (mobile/desktop) to cache prefixes / KV to lower token usage and latency while preserving revocable access.

Assumptions:
- Device has intermittent connectivity and may need to operate with cached prefix windows.
- Customer will authenticate via short-lived device token minted by their backend (standard OIDC + Redwood API key exchange).
- We need a revocable, auditable session bound to a device id and model variant.

High-level handshake sequence (first contact):
1) App calls customer backend: POST /api/devices/register -> returns device_jwt (exp: 10m), device_id.
2) App opens TLS to Redwood Edge (regional) and POST /v1/local/session/handshake with device_jwt, client_meta, desired_model.
3) Edge validates device_jwt via customer OIDC (or Redwood integration), issues session_token (exp short, refreshable), returns session_metadata and initial cache_manifest (empty or delta).
4) App establishes local ephemeral proxy (unix socket / localhost:xxxxx) and binds session_token locally for SDKs.

Sequence diagram (ascii):

App  -> Customer Backend: request device token
App  -> Edge: POST /local/session/handshake (device_jwt)
Edge -> Authz: validate device_jwt
Edge -> App: session_token + manifest + sync_cursor
App  -> Local SDKs: route requests -> local proxy
Local proxy -> Edge: forward cached-aware request (includes sync_cursor)

Message shapes (handshake request):
POST /v1/local/session/handshake
Body:
{
  "device_jwt": "<jwt>",
  "client_meta": {"os":"iOS", "app_version":"1.2.0", "device_id":"abcd"},
  "model": "redwood/large-v1",
  "desired_cache_policy": "aggressive|conservative"
}

Handshake response:
{
  "session_token": "s.tok.ey..",
  "expires_at": "2025-03-02T15:30:00Z",
  "cache_manifest": [ {"prefix_hash":"sha256:...","sequence": 42, "size_tokens": 120}],
  "sync_cursor": "curs:0001",
  "policies": {"can_privacy_cache": "true", "revoke_url": "https://..."}
}

Notes on fields:
- session_token: short-lived bearer, scope: model, device_id, allowed_ops (generate/embeddings). Refresh via POST /v1/local/session/refresh with refresh_token bound to device backend (to avoid exposing long-lived secrets on-device).
- cache_manifest: list of cached segments Edge suggests for local use. Not guaranteed fresh; each item has sequence/version.
- sync_cursor: opaque pointer for incremental cache syncs.

Local request envelope (when proxied):
POST /v1/local/generate (to Edge)
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <session_token>
Body:
{
  "client_request_id": "uuid",
  "prompt": "Hello",
  "cache_directives": {"use_prefix_hash":"sha256:...","allow_fallback": true},
  "sync_cursor": "curs:0001"
}

Edge behavior on proxied request:
- If prefix present and valid -> serve with reduced token charge (tracked internally).
- If mismatch (sequence older) -> return 412 PRECONDITION_FAILED with suggested sync_delta and new sync_cursor.
- If unauthorized scope -> 403 with reason.

Cache sync flow (incremental):
- Client: POST /v1/local/session/sync { sync_cursor }
- Edge: responds with delta bundle (signed manifest + optional encrypted blob) and next_sync_cursor.
- Client applies delta to local LRU store; tracks manifest entries by prefix_hash and sequence.

Security considerations:
- Never store long-lived private keys on device. Use device_jwt short expiry.
- All cache blobs are signed by Edge; optionally encrypted for HSM-bound customers.
- Revocation: session_token is short-lived, but server maintains revocation list; local proxy must poll /v1/local/session/verify or receive push revocation via websocket when online.

Offline operation:
- If offline, local proxy can answer generate calls using local cache and an onboard small model or limited prefix-only expansion (configurable).
- Mark outputs as "generated_offline": true and attach provenance: ["local_cache:v42"].

Config sketch (local proxy config, YAML-like):
local_proxy:
  device_id: abcd
  session_token: s.tok
  model: redwood/large-v1
  cache:
    max_tokens: 20000
    eviction_policy: lru
    allow_offline_generation: true
  sync:
    mode: incremental
    poll_interval_secs: 3600
    burst_retry: 5
  telemetry: 
    disabled: false
    sample_rate: 0.01

Failure modes / edge cases:
- Partial sync: client has prefix but missing following tokens -> must fall back to full request to Edge (inc cost) and update manifest.
- Clock skew: require tolerant expiry checks (±120s).
- Device reuse: if device_id reused by attacker, short expiry + backend revoke required.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to express cost accounting for cached token usage in billing? Add header X-Cache-Tokens-Used? Need product alignment.
- Push vs poll for revocation: prefer push (websocket) for speed, but mobile may not allow persistent sockets. Consider silent push notifications to trigger verification.
- Prefix granularity: token-level vs chunk-level. Tradeoff storage vs hit rate.
- Experimental: allow local quantized tiny models to fall back for short prompts (privileged customers).

Next steps (me):
- Sketch server-side endpoints + auth flows (INF-987). Create a small PoC where proxy can cache a single "greeting" prefix and successfully serve offline.
- Sync with security on signed manifests and offline encryption options.
- Draft a minimal SDK surface so apps can opt-in (0.1): start/stop proxy, check status, grpc/socket interface.

Random notes to self:
- When returning 412, include human-readable "repair_hint" to help SDK update cache smoothly.
- Consider compacting manifest using bloom filters for offline membership checks.

References / mental links:
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/412 (prototype connector)
- JIRA: INF-987 (design epic)

End of scratchpad.

(If I come back to this, convert to a lightweight PRD: actor, journey, constraints, success metrics like p95 reduction in tokens and 99th pct offline coverage.)
